steps.description: 6 stones. Rows 0..2 are DSU nodes 0..2 and columns 0..2 are nodes 3..5, so a stone joins its row node to its column node.
Stone (0,0) links row 0 (node 0) with column 0 (node 3). unionBySize(0, 3): roots 0 and 3. Set 0 is at least as big, so 3 hangs under it.
Stone (0,1) links row 0 (node 0) with column 1 (node 4). unionBySize(0, 4): roots 0 and 4. Set 0 is at least as big, so 4 hangs under it.
Stone (1,0) links row 1 (node 1) with column 0 (node 3). unionBySize(1, 3): roots 1 and 0. Set 0 is bigger, so 1 hangs under it.
Stone (1,2) links row 1 (node 1) with column 2 (node 5). unionBySize(1, 5): roots 0 and 5. Set 0 is at least as big, so 5 hangs under it.
Stone (2,1) links row 2 (node 2) with column 1 (node 4). unionBySize(2, 4): roots 2 and 0. Set 0 is bigger, so 2 hangs under it.
Stone (2,2) links row 2 (node 2) with column 2 (node 5). unionBySize(2, 5): both have root 0, so they are already in one set - return.
Node 0 (r0) is used by a stone and is its own parent: the root of group 1.
Each group of stones can be removed down to its last one: 6 - 1 = 5.
